sources.evidence: We ranked six streamers by how each one plays from Plex, Navidrome and Jellyfin.
Lightweight, fast and self-contained. Runs well even on resource-limited platforms (ex: Raspberry Pi)
Plays well with gigantic music collections (tested with ~900K songs - 2/3 FLAC, 1/3 MP3)
Very low resource usage . Runs well even on simple Raspberry Pi Zero and old hardware setups Handles very large music collections
The Synology DS225+ is our top pick for music storage. It offers 282 MB/s transfer speeds, Intel hardware transcoding, and Synology Audio Station for built-in music streaming.

sources.why: Generic NAS setup, no model picks
sources.evidence: For anyone with more than a few hundred albums, a two-bay NAS with two drives in a mirror is the right home for the music
Navidrome and gonic run comfortably on a Raspberry Pi. Funkwhale and Jellyfin need a real server with 2-4 GB of RAM.
run Navidrome on a 1 vCPU / 1 GB VPS with enough disk for your library, pair it with a Subsonic client such as Symfonium or play:Sub
Best overall Navidrome Lightweight, fast, Subsonic API compatible, runs on anything Best for federation/social Funkwhale
Navidrome is the better dedicated music server. It’s lighter, free, and gives you access to 50+ polished Subsonic-compatible music apps.
A place to store the files — usually a NAS (network-attached storage box) or a spare computer.

missing: Specific NAS models compared on Navidrome/Plex Docker support, CPU and RAM for library scanning and FLAC transcoding (Plexamp in particular), drive bays, current prices and a direct pick.
why: No major reviewer or authority picks NAS hardware for this question. Navidrome's own pages are about the software, and most other results compare server software, streamers or VPS hosting. The only page that names NAS models is lockah.net, an affiliate listicle with no testing. A focused page comparing NAS models for Navidrome and Plexamp, with prices, would face little competition.
